name: m4
why: A classic Unix macro language that can be pushed into surprisingly odd territory, though it is widely known in build systems.

brief.what_it_is: GNU M4 is an implementation of the traditional Unix macro processor. It reads input, copies it to output, and expands macros as it goes, where macros are either builtin or user-defined and can take any number of arguments. Beyond expansion, it has builtin functions for including named files, running Unix shell commands, integer arithmetic, and text manipulation. It can be used as a front-end to a compiler or as a standalone macro processor.
brief.why_it_exists: The page presents GNU M4 as a GNU implementation of the classic Unix macro processor, mostly SVR4 compatible with some extensions such as handling more than 9 positional parameters to macros. It is also described as a major dependency of the GNU Autoconf project.
brief.how_it_works: m4 copies its input to the output and expands macros as it encounters them. Macros can be builtin or user-defined and accept any number of arguments. Builtin functions cover file inclusion, shell command execution, integer arithmetic, and text manipulation.

brief.install_notes: No Homebrew-specific notes on the page. The page lists the latest stable version as 1.4.20, available as a release from https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/m4/ or an FTP mirror. Source can also be taken from git, with the stable branch-1.4 checked out as shown in commands_seen. No hardware, accounts, or runtime requirements are mentioned. Building from source is implied by the git and CVS options, but the page gives no build steps.
brief.standout: Its own extensions and history set it apart from a simple macro expander: it includes shell execution, arithmetic, and file inclusion as builtins, and it is still the engine under GNU Autoconf. The page also says version 2.0 is planned with better input control, multiple precision arithmetic, and loadable modules.
brief.status: Maintained. The page lists stable release 1.4.20, and the manual page says it was last updated May 10, 2025. It names two maintainers, Gary V. Vaughan and Eric Blake, and points to active development on Savannah. I could not find an exact release date for 1.4.20.
brief.caveats: The page says test versions should not be used in production. The 2.0 features it describes (better input control, multiple precision arithmetic, loadable modules, translations) are future plans, not current features. The mailing lists are moderated because of spam, so posts may be held for a while before they appear. Development is volunteer-driven. The homepage gives no usage examples; the manual is linked but its page only lists download formats, so I did not see macro examples.
quotes: GNU M4 is an implementation of the traditional Unix macro processor.
m4 can be used either as a front-end to a compiler or as a macro processor in its own right.
One of the biggest users of GNU M4 is the GNU Autoconf project.
Please remember that development of GNU M4 is a volunteer effort, and you can also contribute to its development.
